description: De Staat der Nederlanden nodigt u als potentiële inschrijver uit om in te schrijven voor de openbare Europese aanbesteding voor de aanschaf van een SAAS-oplossing inzake constructiesoftware voor het kunnen maken en beheren van examenvragen voor de Wet Financieel Toezicht (hierna: Wft). Doel is het afsluiten van een dienstverleningsovereenkomst met één leverancier. The tenure types are to be split by block. Delivery of 900m2 of commercial property split over 3 selected ground floor locations across KUC-S1, KUC-S2 and KUC-S3 to facilitate employment or retail use within the wider development. Progress site identification for 6300 m2 of employment use for future development. A location for the employment use has been identified on the included schematic, this does not have to be the final location. The Council is seeking to identify an economic operator that has the requisite skillset and is considered most capable of working in collaboration with the Council, to identify the optimal solution for the development site in accordance with the SDZ and the Council’s requirement and to deliver it as efficiently as possible.

title: France – Installation of telecommunications equipment – ACBC - RVT – TELECOM – Partie Télécom (multi territoire) - 6 lots
description: Accord-cadre multi-attributaire à bons de commande, passé sans engagement de commande et sans montant minimum, avec un montant maximum par lot, portant sur des travaux de télécommunications ferroviaires. Il est décomposé en 6 lots géographiques : Lot PACA, Lot LANGUEDOC ROUSSILLON, Lot RHONE, Lot ALPES, Lot AUVERGNE NIVERNAIS et Lot BOURGOGNE FRANCHE COMPTE. Les travaux comprennent notamment : l’aménagement de locaux télécoms (baies, coffrets, têtes de câbles optiques, chemins de câbles, mise à la terre) ; l’aménagement des prises et tableaux de distribution d’énergie ; le déroulage, le raccordement et les tests de câbles courants faibles (cuivre, LAN, fibre optique) ; le déroulage et le raccordement de câbles courants forts alimentant les installations télécoms ; la pose d’équipements télécoms en gare et sur quai (écrans de téléaffichage, caméras, haut-parleurs, balises sonores, horloges, bornes wifi, antennes, supports et mâts) ; la pose de fourreaux et tubes PEHD, de câbles cuivre et de fibres optiques ; la confection de prises de terre et de terres longitudinales ; les travaux de petit génie civil associés (massifs, fourreaux, percements, bris de béton). Les détails sont précisés au DCE. Chaque lot est attribué à deux titulaires : le titulaire de rang 1 (mieux-disant) et le titulaire de rang 2 (second mieux-disant). Les bons de commande sont répartis en montant à hauteur de 70 % (± 10 %) pour le titulaire de rang 1 et de 30 % (± 10 %) pour le titulaire de rang 2, sur chaque période d’exécution. Cette répartition s’applique aux bons de commande effectivement émis et ne constitue pas un engagement de volume. Le montant de chaque bon de commande est plafonné à 200 000 € HT. L’accord-cadre comprend une tranche ferme de 2 ans, du 10/05/2027 au 09/05/2029, et une reconduction éventuelle d’un an, du 10/05/2029 au 09/05/2030. Les candidats peuvent candidater à un ou plusieurs lots. Un même soumissionnaire ne peut être attributaire de plus de 2 lots en rang 1 et de plus de 2 lots en rang 2, selon les règles précisées dans le règlement de consultation.

title: Norway – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – Loppa municipality - Molo - Øksfjord Harbour
description: On behalf of Loppa municipality, tenderers are invited to a competition for improvements to the port conditions in Øksfjord. The General contract (NS 8406) includes the establishment of two new piers, the establishment of a new pumping station, a sewage pipeline and an access road. Dredging the seabed under Molo South is necessary to ensure sufficient geotechnical stability before completion. Dredging masses shall be reused as core masses in the piers and for filling ditches, while any surplus matter is delivered to an approved site. The work shall be carried out with environmental measures such as bubble curtain and turbidity monitoring. The existing sewage pipeline must have been moved and relaid with a new pumping station before sea work starts. The pier North shall be partially established before dredging starts to enable encapsulation of the dredging masses and reduce particle dispersion. The contract includes further filling work, width expansion and extension of Pier North, establishment of a turnaround, as well as concrete work on a new and existing pier. The concrete works are options and include casting breakwater covers, parapets and casting on existing constructions. The builder is free to order all or parts of the optioned concrete works. The execution shall be carried out in accordance with the engineering design documentation and the accompanying drawings. Furthermore, there are option posts for the demolition and re-establishment of approx. 200 metres of existing sewage pipeline on land.

title: Data & AI Mission Expert Services (DAMES) IDIQ
description: The Department of the Air Force Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Officer (DAF CDAO in SAF/CND) is conducting market intelligence to identify sources for a potential requirement for Data & AI Mission Expert Services (DAMES) IDIQ support services in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement. The Government is still in the early acquisition planning stage and all activities at this time are considered market intelligence. This is a Request for Information (RFI) and is NOT a request for proposals and the information received will be utilized for acquisition planning purposes. Responders are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred with response to this announcement and information submitted in response to this RFI will not be returned. 1.0 REQUESTED INFORMATION 1.1 Capability Statement: Request you submit a capability statement that presents your technical capability for completing the attached Performance Work Statement. The capability statement shall at a minimum address the specific items below. 1.1.1 Approach: Describe your approach for accomplishing the Performance Work Statement. 1.1.2 Past Performance: Identify previous contracts which are relevant to the scope of the Performance Work Statement. Include contract number, period of performance, whether performance was completed as a prime or subcontract, and a summary of services provided. 1.1.3 Timeline: Attached your timeline in obtaining the required skill set for contract award. This timeline should include time for any applicable transition period, clearances (if required), and any other information that would be crucial to successfully transition to contract award. 1.1.4 Page Limit: Capability Statements are limited to 15 pages in total length, single spaced, and 12-point font and accessible by either Microsoft Word or Adobe Acrobat. 1.2 Submission Instructions: Please provide your responses to this RFI to the primary POC listed in this announcement by the timeframe listed in this announcement. Additionally, please include your company's CAGE, Unique Entity ID, and Size Standard as part of your submission. Please note: Large submissions may be required to be sent via multiple e-mails. The Government recommends contacting the primary POC in this announcement to verify receipt. 1.3 Industry Discussions: The Government may choose to meet with companies who responded to this RFI to hold one-on-one discussions. Discussions would only be held to obtain further clarification of potential capability to meet the requirement. 1.4 Proposed Acquisition Strategy: The Government is contemplating using the Highest Technically Rated Offeror (HRTO) selection methodology for this acquisition. This allows the Government to promote efficiency in acquisition through a streamlined selection decision, especially for this knowledge based services where technical ability is of paramount concern. The Government would like to solicit industry feedback for this acquisition approach regarding the pros/cons that industry perceives with the acquisition approach. 1.5 Industry Feedback Regarding Requirement: While the Government is the final decision regarding the requirement, we would like to solicit industry feedback regarding the attached requirements documentation and where industry thinks that we could improve the overall quality of the product/service received by updating/clarifying our requirement.

description: GUSG HABITAT HYDRO-LOGIC RESTORATION 2026 AMENDMENT 1 09/10/2026- This amendment is to reopen and extend the due date to 09/14/2026 12pm (noon) MD. description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. All parts must have clear traceability to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Aero Rubber Co Inc. (Cage Code: 64665). title: United States Army Western Hemisphere Command (USAWHC) G-6 Information Technology Service Management Western Command and Control System (WCCS)
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small businesses and large businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services. USAWHC G-6 seeks information from potential sources for comprehensive Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) support for the WCCS. Established as the Army�s theater-level headquarters supporting both U.S. Northern Command and U.S. Southern Command, USAWHC unifies former United States Army North and United States Army South capabilities into a single four-star command executing homeland defense, defense support to civil authorities, and theater security cooperation across North America, Latin America, and the Caribbean. In support of this newly formed Theater Army for the Americas, HQ USAWHC G-6 requires comprehensive ITSM solutions to deliver and sustain critical command and control (C2), Unified Communications (UC), Audio/Visual (AV), and enterprise information technology (IT) capabilities. Scope of support spans HQ USAWHC (Fort Liberty/Camp Mackall), Joint Base San Antonio, and associated remote/Deployable Communications Element (DCE) locations, encompassing program management, service desk/information management operations (IMO), data center and network operations, asset accountability, knowledge management, and full-spectrum cybersecurity�including Risk Management Framework (RMF)/Authority to Operate sustainment, vulnerability management, incident response, and communications security operations (COMSEC) accountability.

description: U.S. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY Request for Information (RFI) Regarding the Next Generation of EPA�s Superfund Remediation Acquisition Framework (RAF) Contracts Attachment, "RFI - Body" includes identical information as found below, however may be more easily read from a formatting standpoint. Request for Information (RFI) The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is posting these draft requirements (see attachments) and questions to obtain feedback from industry to help shape the next generation of contracts supporting the Superfund Remedial Program. EPA�s goal is to increase the performance-based aspects of the requirements, providing more flexibility to contractors in how work is performed while ensuring EPA receives the necessary services/deliverables. Contractors are welcome to make Track Changes within the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) and resubmit recommendations back to the agency for consideration. Additionally, EPA has included a list of questions below on specific topics for feedback. It is the Government�s intent to use the recommendations and feedback received from industry to help better inform the strategic direction of the procurement process (e.g. requirement refinement, improvement, or clarification), but is under no obligation to incorporate any proposed changes into the final PWS. All information and documentation posted under this notice is preliminary in nature and may be updated or amended prior to the release of the formal solicitation. The agency intends to post draft solicitations for each requirement at a later date for industry questions and/or feedback. Additionally, EPA is developing an external-facing website to enable future posting of information and facilitate communication. It is EPA�s hope the website will be used not only to facilitate communication between EPA and industry regarding the next generation of contracts, but also be a useful resource for intra-industry communication for Prime/Sub relationship building. A future notification will be posted when the external website is operational. This notice does not constitute a formal solicitation. Once a solicitation is posted, all responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by the agency. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this notice; all costs associated with responding to this notice will solely be at the interested parties� expense. Any information provided by industry to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation(s). The questions in this RFI are for market research and information-gathering purposes only. They do not reflect final agency requirements, preferences, or decisions, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Agency to any particular acquisition strategy, scope, contract type, or solicitation content. Basic information on the current Remedial Acquisition Framework (RAF) program and contracts is located at https://www.epa.gov/superfund/remedial-acquisition-framework. description:
L’Université Bastion à Genève fait l’objet d’un projet global de rénovation visant une transformation à la fois architecturale et fonctionnelle de l’ensemble existant. L’objectif des travaux est une revalorisation durable de la structure bâtie, en tenant compte des exigences actuelles en matière d’architecture, d’usage, de technique et d’efficacité énergétique.


L’accent est mis sur le développement respectueux du patrimoine bâti historique, tout en intégrant des standards contemporains sur le plan des infrastructures et de l’expression architecturale. Dans ce contexte, des aspects tels que la qualité des espaces, la flexibilité des usages ainsi qu’une approche architecturale claire jouent un rôle central.


Les travaux ont d’ores et déjà débuté et l’exploitation du site se poursuit actuellement dans un contexte de chantier en cours. La mise en service est prévue pour l’année académique 2027 / 2028.


Cet appel d'offre se déroulera en deux phases. Au premier tour, les soumissionnaires devront fournir les documents demandés ainsi que les échantillons de la lentille et du support en métal, selon les indications de l'appel d'offres. Après analyse des dossiers transmis, 3 candidats seront sélectionnés et invités à participer à la 2e phase en fonction des critères de sélection.

description: The Ladner Small Craft Harbour in Ladner, BC, requires maintenance dredging services. The scope of work may also include float and wharf repairs as optional items. Familiarization with site: Before submitting a bid, bidders can visit the site and its surroundings, at their own expense, to review and verify the form, nature, and extent of the work, materials needed for the completion of the work, the means of access to the site, severity, exposure, and uncertainty of weather, soil conditions, any accommodations they may require, and in general shall obtain all necessary information as to risks, contingencies, and other circumstances which may influence or affect their bid. All work including clean-up and demobilization must be completed by February 28, 2027.

description: Atlantic Technological University (ATU) seeks tenders for the appointment of a suitable contractor for the development and construction of a Veterinary Medical Facility at Atlantic Technological University (ATU), Knocknamona, Letterkenny, Co Donegal. The facility is intended to provide modern clinical, teaching and research facilities, incorporating small-animal, large-animal and equine functions together with pathology, animal accommodation, external yards and associated infrastructure. title: Supply of Army Branded Clothing
description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform. The authority requires the supply of a standardised package of Army-branded clothing. Providing practical, recognisable and consistent clothing for public-facing recruitment and engagement events, routine travel and outdoor activity. A consistent clothing package is required to improve professional presentation, support Army branding and provide practical clothing suitable for the environments in which the teams operate. Provide a consistent and professional Army identity across Arms & Services Engagement Teams. Provide practical clothing suitable for travel, public events and outdoor engagement activity. Deliver a one-off issue that requires no ongoing maintenance, repair or replacement commitment from the Authority. Included: manufacture, Army branding, packaging and delivery of complete clothing packages in the sizes confirmed by the Authority. Included: one coordinated delivery, unless an alternative delivery schedule is agreed in writing by the Authority. Excluded: recurring supply, replacement for loss or damage, repair, laundering, alteration after acceptance, and ongoing stock management. Requirements The Contractor shall provide complete clothing packages. Each package shall contain: One quilted puffer jacket. One softshell jacket. One pair of stretch trousers. Three moisture-wicking T-shirts. Three pairs of physical training shorts. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest and can also be found at the link attached. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title "TSS 809 Opportunity"

title: Debris Boom Supply and Install at Harry S. Truman Lake Project
description: The solicitation is amended to provide revisions to the Purchase Description, CLIN Structure, provide a Projnet Plan Room key to access the Bathymetry survey information and extend the quote due date. Also, Contractor Questions Answered Part 2 are posted. Contractor Questions/Government Answers are posted. The purpose of the debris boom is to prevent floating debris from impacting the dam's tainter gates, which is crucial for maintaining the full operational capacity of the spillway. The boom will also serve as a visual barrier to boaters. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, engineering, fabrication, delivery, and optional installation necessary to furnish a complete debris boom system at Harry S. Truman Dam. The approximately 2,000-foot boom shall be designed to intercept floating debris upstream of the spillway and withstand site-specific hydraulic, wind, wave, debris, and impact loading conditions. The debris boom shall be designed for an 800-foot-long by 3-foot-thick debris field, use a minimum safety factor of 2.0 for design loads, withstand a direct head-on impact from an 18-inch-diameter, 100-foot-long log traveling at the maximum design water velocity, and withstand design conditions including 50 mph wind speed and 5-foot wave height. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns and is competed as full and open competition, Unrestricted. An organized site visit has been scheduled for: Friday, 9 October 2026 at 11am.

description: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) to obtain a Medicare Administrative Contractor (hereinafter referred to as �the contractor�) to provide specified health insurance benefit administration services, including Medicare claims processing and payment services, in support of the Medicare Program (also known as the Medicare Fee-For-Service or FFS) for Jurisdiction 8. Jurisdiction 8 encompasses the following states: Indiana and Michigan. Prior to issuing the final solicitation, with this synopsis CMS is issuing a draft RFP (inclusive of the RFP and attachments) to allow potential offerors an opportunity to review the requirements and submit questions. Consistent with the statement of work, the contractor shall perform numerous functions to support healthcare services for Medicare beneficiaries, which include performing claims-related activities and establishing relationships with providers of Medicare services, both institutional and professional, both in-patient (Part A) and out-patient (Part B). The contractor will perform the requirements of this contract in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, Medicare manuals, as well as CMS requirements to ensure the financial integrity of the Medicare FFS Program. Pursuant to the authority of FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation, CMS intends to conduct a full and open procurement to fulfill this need. Accordingly, the Contracting Officer will seek to award to the vendor whose proposal represents the best solution to CMS� requirements at a fair and reasonable price. Award will be made to the Offeror whose proposal offers the best overall value to the Government using FAR 15.103-1 Trade-off approach, which ��is appropriate when it may be in the Government�s best interest to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror ��; affording the Government the most advantageous balance of cost and technical factors as defined in the upcoming solicitation. title: Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) Support Services
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD) is soliciting for scientific, engineering, and technical services required for the design, development, fabrication, integration, test, fleet implementation, and maintenance of Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) based simulation systems. The Government requires support system installations and updates required for the following five categories of Navy fleet training systems: Submarine Team, Navigation, Surface, Surveillance, and On-Board. The Government requires design, development, integration, testing, delivery, installation, and maintenance of fielded systems. The Government requires technical engineering support for simulation and training system capabilities to existing fleet onsite maintenance personnel for the operational systems. The Government also requires support for tactical testing and analysis system configurations for common simulation and tactical subsystems utilized in these trainers. The Government is soliciting this requirement as full-and-open competition. The contract will be awarded as a single award indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity(IDIQ), with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort (LOE) CLINs and Cost Only Other Direct Costs (ODCs) CLINs for incidental materials and travel. The contract will be for a period of three years to include three one-year ordering periods.

description: This is a sources sought notice for information only. This sources sought is for the purpose of conducting market research to provide data for planning purposes. This sources sought synopsis announcement does not constitute a formal solicitation, and is not a request for proposal, request for quote, invitation for bid, does not obligate the government to award a contract, issue a solicitation, reimburse respondents for any proposal preparation and/or submittal costs, nor does its issuance in any way restrict the Government as to its ultimate acquisition approach. The Government will not pay for any materials provided in response to this notice and submittals will not be returned to the sender. The U.S. Department of State (DoS) is the lead institution for the conduct of American diplomacy with its mission to advance U.S. national security interests, fight terrorism, protect U.S. interests abroad, and implement foreign policy initiatives that build a freer, more prosperous, and secure world. The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL), works to keep Americans safe at home by countering international crime, illegal drugs, and instability abroad. In Honduras, INL assists the host government by strengthening police, prosecutors, and judges. These efforts reduce the amount of crime and illegal drugs reaching U.S. shores keeping American communities safe while enhancing Honduras' capacity to deliver security and justice services to its citizens. INL's work in Honduras supports the country's efforts to combat transnational criminal organizations and disrupt U.S.-bound illicit drugs. The Contractor shall refurbish an approximate area of 335 m�, including the demolition of existing elements, redistribution of spaces, construction of new divisions, installation of electrical systems and necessary adaptations to guarantee optimal operating conditions. Remodeling should follow all technical specifications stated on approved designs. All mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems shall be installed within the walls, floors, shafts, and/or above finished ceilings. Exposed surface mounted plumbing and electrical components will only be approved on a case-by-case basis. Walls shall be plastered per commercial industry standards and cured before applying surface coatings. Contractor shall not deviate from the design approved by INL and the Client without their prior approval. The contractor must execute all works in accordance with good civil engineering practices, technical standards applicable in Honduras (including criteria used by FHIS and local building regulations), as well as international quality standards in interior works. All materials must be new, of the highest quality and suitable for the intended use. The use of defective materials, reused without authorization or that do not comply with technical specifications will not be allowed. The contractor will be responsible for verifying on-site dimensions, existing conditions, and compatibility between systems before executing any activity. The project shall be constructed according to the plans, specifications and the list of requirements provided below. This is not a solicitation, nor will a solicitation package be issued as a result of this announcement, and no award shall be made as a result of this announcement. In the event that a solicitation is developed, it will be assigned a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) number or Request for Quotation (RFQ) and the announcement will be published on SAM.gov. RESPONSES DUE For the purposes of this acquisition the applicable NAICS code is 236220. Responses are requested no later than 02 November 2026 at 12:00 PM EST. Direct expression of interest as well as required documentation should be submitted in writing, via email, to Joonpil Hwang at hwangj2@state.gov and David M. Scott at ScottDM@state.gov. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring this site for the release of all other information pertaining to the synopsis and solicitation. RESPONSE SUBMISSION INFORMATION All potential sources with the capability to provide the requirements referenced in this sources sought are invited to submit, in writing, sufficient information within the page limitations listed below. This information should demonstrate the respondent's ability to fulfill the technical, delivery, and support requirements and be responsive to the technical questions in this RFI as indicated below. We will not answer technical questions or provide additional technical information at this time via this sources sought notice. Please understand that the rough order of magnitude is for the purposes of market research and your firm will in no way be committed to any estimate you provide under this notice. Responses to this RFI shall include the following: 1. A cover sheet which includes: Company Name Address Point of Contact E-mail Address Phone Number UEI Number Primary Business and Market Areas Business Size and Socioeconomic Status (if applicable) 2. Relevant Construction Project Experience (four (4) page limit): The potential offerors need to demonstrate that they possess, within the last five years, construction experience similar to that described in this specified source sought category in Honduras. Offerors must verify experience commensurate with renovation/refurbishment of buildings/facilities. Experience described above needs to include the offeror�s role, primary contractor or sub-contractor. Each project experience needs to include the contract number, the US Agency or private company that awarded the contract and contract monetary value. Potential offerors shall be licensed and certified to perform architectural, engineering, and construction services in Honduras. Copies of the licenses and certifications must be submitted in response to the sources sought and are excluded from the two (2) page limit. Submit copies of such licenses. The potential offerors need to document experience in coordinating with host nation government(s) to mitigate and solve potential issues; Experience in importation of materials, equipment, manpower, and any other necessary resources required for the completion of design-build projects; 3. Capabilities of Successfully Completing Construction (six (6) page limit): Ability to provide all required design and engineering services, manpower, and materials to construct new buildings or to renovate existing ones; Ability to provide and deliver required materials and equipment to projects located in Honduras; Capabilities to import all required material and equipment through either sea or air transportation to Honduras; Ability that, should a solicitation be issued in the future for this requirement, offerors should declare if the offeror is applying as a primary contractor, a joint venture or partnership or other as applicable to their submission. title: AFLCMC/HNIT seeks expressions of interest regarding a potential commercial coworking space in the environs of Concord, Massachusetts.
description: The purpose of this request for information is to seek responses from interested vendors regarding a potential short-term commercial coworking space service contract for the Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS) program, which the agency anticipates that it may award in the summer of 2027. The projected period of performance start date is August 2, 2027. The agency seeks, in particular, responses from vendors that meet the requirements listed below. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) has been attached to this notice, which provides additional information on the required services. Responses should clearly indicate whether the vendor believes that it can meet all requirements. If it believes that it cannot, the vendor should specifically identify the requirements that it believes it can meet and those that it believes it cannot meet. Where possible, the vendor shall indicate and describe the particular property or properties that it believes would be suited to this contract, and the nature of its interest in that property (if any). The agency anticipates, in accordance with Department of the Air Force (DAF) Contract Policy Memo 24-C-10, that the PSC shall be X1AB (Lease/Rental of Conference Space and Facilities) and the NAICS shall be 531120. Note that this service contract, if awarded, will be in full accordance with the requirements set forth in the memo. Property Management: The contractor shall provide an environment that meets the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement. It shall be approximately within a 6-mile radius of the Concord Town House, 22 Monument Square, Concord, MA (with the approximate coordinates being 42�27'40.1"N 71�20'55.0"W). (The agency may consider an environment outside of this 6-mile radius if it determines that it is in its best interest to do so.) It shall have roughly 30,000 square feet of office space; it shall contain 190 or more workstations, 6 to 8 private �office pods� or �booths� (each of a size sufficient to accommodate one individual), 4 small collaborative spaces (each of a size sufficient to accommodate up to 6 individuals), a commercial lactation pod, and 6 to 8 meeting rooms, with a personnel range of 151-175 individuals when fully operational, and potentially 176-200 individuals to meet future programmatic demands. It shall have a break area/dining area and a shared kitchen area that meet the requirements specified in the PWS. The parking lot or garage shall have a capacity sufficient for all personnel. Within the coworking space, the contractor shall provide a dedicated, private, exclusive fully enclosed office for the operational use of authorized DAF personnel, which meets the security, structural, and other specifications listed in the PWS. IT Support and Maintenance Services: The vendor shall provide IT support for the coworking space�s workstations and conference equipment. It shall provide on-site technical support staffing. It shall monitor the equipment and the IT infrastructure to ensure that equipment is free from defects, that equipment is operable, and that connectivity is maintained. If the vendor observes any actual or potential information security violations in the course of providing this support, it shall report them to the Government Security Manager. Administrative and Janitorial Services: The vendor shall ensure that restrooms are restocked and maintained, that the shared kitchen and kitchen appliances are maintained, that shared kitchen supplies are restocked (including the restocking of the commercial coffee machine and beverage dispenser), that meeting rooms, open seating areas, and other elements of the coworking space are maintained, shall provide front desk staffing, and shall otherwise administer the coworking space in accordance with commercial practices and with agency-specific needs. Software Licenses, Collaboration Licenses, Network Services, Power/Utility Services, and Commercial Wi-Fi: The contractor shall provide these services in accordance with the PWS. Hardware and Enclosures: The contractor shall install and maintain contractor-owned or contractor-leased hardware and equipment (e.g. printers) and shall install and maintain government-owned hardware and equipment (e.g. large-format displays and computer monitors) in accordance with the PWS. It shall permit the installation of a lockable, ventilated, government-owned IT equipment rack or wall-mounted communications cabinet within the dedicated space. This notice is not a solicitation and does not bind the agency in any way. If the agency opts to post a solicitation, it will only consider those bidders that are actively registered on SAM.gov at the time of issuance of the solicitation. Responses are due by 12:00 PM EDT on October 27, 2026, and should be emailed to Contract Specialist Steven C. Bodnar at steven.bodnar@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist Andrew C. St. Maurice at andrew.st_maurice@us.af.mil.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE RELATED TO SEVERAL UPCOMING PROJECTS at WRIGHT-PATTERSON AFB, OHIO
description: ***21 October 2026 Update: The responses due date is being revised to 02 Novemeber at 12:00 P.M. Eastern Time. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE RELATED TO SEVERAL UPCOMING PROJECTS at WPAFB, OHIO Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) 1. PROJECT OVERVIEWS The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), in support of the United States Air Force (USAF), is conducting market research to identify interested and qualified industry partners for the design and construction of several upcoming construction projects at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. PROJECT 1: RENOVATE NASIC MAIN CAMPUS, PHASE 1, F/10853 - This project is renovation of 170,000 SF of Sensitive and/or Special Access Program spaces. The work consists of the full renovation of F/10853 through reconfiguration and interior renovation to create a network of administrative functions. The work shall be done in accordance with Intelligence Community Directive 705 (ICD 705) criteria and standards. The interior demolition consists of removal of all architectural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) elements including floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. Work includes replacement of building systems, reconfiguration of interior partitions, life safety systems, roof replacement, and envelope modification. The roofing system will be replaced with an energy-compliant system. Penetrations will be added to the building for daylighting, and the exterior envelope will be modified on first floor locations for mechanical rooms. All piping and sprinklers that are part of the current fire protection system are to be replaced. All domestic water, storm, and sanitary piping will be replaced. Additionally, this project includes cybersecurity measures. A corridor bridge connecting F/10828 and F/10856 over an existing loading dock is to be constructed. Personnel will require swing space during the renovation of F/10853. Swing space will be provided through existing available spaces throughout the NASIC IPC campus or via a temporary facility. It is critical that the sequencing of repair work be considered so that available spaces are not overwhelmed. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $160,000,000 PROJECT 2: Advanced Materials Research Laboratory � C2A - Construction of an approximately ~90,000 SF three-story laboratory and research facility, as well as the potential construction of a central utility plant for the Air Force Reach Labor Material and Manufacturing Directorate. New facility will consist of concrete, foundation, structural steel frame, masonry etc. Onsite gas boilers for heat and chilled water generation for cooling and lab processes. The interior shall consist of open inter-disciplinary collaboration labs with clean utilities, vibration isolation, precision HVAC and humidity controls, as well as fire protection/suppression, intrusion detections systems and medium voltage switchgear (i.e. 12,470 volts). Site work consists of utilities, sidewalks, parking, communications The new facility shall connect to existing facilities and demolitions of facility 20654. is part of this project. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $122,000,000 PROJECT 3: Compressor Research Facility Systems Modernization This project will modernize the Air Force Research Lab�s (AFRL) Compressor Research Facility (CRF) by replacing legacy drive and power equipment with a new 30,000-horsepower Variable Frequency Drive system to support engine component testing. The effort will deliver a fully integrated system that improves reliability, control, maintainability, and long-term test capability. Work includes replacement of the existing drive system with a new 30,000-horsepower VFD with active front end, a new 30,000-horsepower brushless synchronous motor, a new primary transformer, medium-voltage switchgear, protective relaying, and all associated interconnecting cables, bus work, grounding, and terminations. The project also includes the demolition and removal of legacy electrical and mechanical equipment; upgrades to controls, monitoring interfaces, cooling and ventilation systems, and supporting electrical infrastructure; and any required structural, foundation, enclosure, or fire/life-safety modifications needed to install and operate the new equipment. Additional work will include system integration, testing, commissioning, performance verification, operator and maintainer training, and delivery of technical data, recommended spare parts, and warranty support. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $25,000,000 PROJECT 4: Consolidate/Demo F/31240 This project will decentralize Area A heating by replacing the aging high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system fed from Building F/31240, Line A, and Line D with standalone boiler plants serving 49 facilities. The project supports administrative, warehouse, laboratory, hangar, and dormitory buildings that require year-round hot water for heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. Work includes facility surveys, evaluation of mechanical room capacity and code compliance, and determination of any needed interior renovations or limited additions to support the new equipment. The project also includes demolition of Building F/31240 and its boiler equipment, removal of above-ground HTHW piping and supports, and capping and abandonment of below-grade piping in place. New high-efficiency boiler systems, pumps, controls, and related accessories will be installed at affected facilities, with evaluation of both natural gas-fired and electric options. Additional work includes mechanical room modifications, make-up water assemblies where needed, upgrades to electrical, fire alarm, fire suppression, and direct digital control systems, and site restoration including pavement repair, grass restoration, and backfill and seeding at the demolished plant site. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $66,500,000 PROJECT 5: Consolidate/Demo West Ramp This project will decentralize heating for the West Ramp area at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base by replacing the existing high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system from Building F/34019 with standalone boiler plants serving 15 surrounding facilities. The effort addresses aging and degraded infrastructure supporting administrative, laboratory, and active hangar facilities that require year-round hot water for comfort heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. The project includes surveying each facility to determine boiler locations, evaluating mechanical room walls for code compliance, and assessing whether mechanical room expansions, electrical upgrades, or system improvements are needed to support the new equipment. description: This is a sources sought notice for information only. This sources sought is for the purpose of conducting market research to provide data for planning purposes. This sources sought synopsis announcement does not constitute a formal solicitation, and is not a request for proposal, request for quote, invitation for bid, does not obligate the government to award a contract, issue a solicitation, reimburse respondents for any proposal preparation and/or submittal costs, nor does its issuance in any way restrict the Government as to its ultimate acquisition approach. The Government will not pay for any materials provided in response to this notice and submittals will not be returned to the sender. The U.S. Department of State (DoS) is the lead institution for the conduct of American diplomacy with its mission to advance U.S. national security interests, fight terrorism, protect U.S. interests abroad, and implement foreign policy initiatives that build a freer, more prosperous, and secure world. The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL), works to keep Americans safe at home by countering international crime, illegal drugs, and instability abroad. In Honduras, INL assists the host government by strengthening police, prosecutors, and judges. These efforts reduce the amount of crime and illegal drugs reaching U.S. shores keeping American communities safe while enhancing Honduras' capacity to deliver security and justice services to its citizens. INL's work in Honduras supports the country's efforts to combat transnational criminal organizations and disrupt U.S.-bound illicit drugs. The Contractor shall refurbish an approximate area of 335 m�, including the demolition of existing elements, redistribution of spaces, construction of new divisions, installation of electrical systems and necessary adaptations to guarantee optimal operating conditions. Remodeling should follow all technical specifications stated on approved designs. All mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems shall be installed within the walls, floors, shafts, and/or above finished ceilings. Exposed surface mounted plumbing and electrical components will only be approved on a case-by-case basis. Walls shall be plastered per commercial industry standards and cured before applying surface coatings. Contractor shall not deviate from the design approved by INL and the Client without their prior approval. The contractor must execute all works in accordance with good civil engineering practices, technical standards applicable in Honduras (including criteria used by FHIS and local building regulations), as well as international quality standards in interior works. All materials must be new, of the highest quality and suitable for the intended use. The use of defective materials, reused without authorization or that do not comply with technical specifications will not be allowed. The contractor will be responsible for verifying on-site dimensions, existing conditions, and compatibility between systems before executing any activity. The project shall be constructed according to the plans, specifications and the list of requirements provided below. This is not a solicitation, nor will a solicitation package be issued as a result of this announcement, and no award shall be made as a result of this announcement. title: AFLCMC/HNIT seeks expressions of interest regarding a potential commercial coworking space in the environs of Concord, Massachusetts.
description: The purpose of this request for information is to seek responses from interested vendors regarding a potential short-term commercial coworking space service contract for the Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS) program, which the agency anticipates that it may award in the summer of 2027. The projected period of performance start date is August 2, 2027. The agency seeks, in particular, responses from vendors that meet the requirements listed below. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) has been attached to this notice, which provides additional information on the required services. Responses should clearly indicate whether the vendor believes that it can meet all requirements. If it believes that it cannot, the vendor should specifically identify the requirements that it believes it can meet and those that it believes it cannot meet. Where possible, the vendor shall indicate and describe the particular property or properties that it believes would be suited to this contract, and the nature of its interest in that property (if any). The agency anticipates, in accordance with Department of the Air Force (DAF) Contract Policy Memo 24-C-10, that the PSC shall be X1AB (Lease/Rental of Conference Space and Facilities) and the NAICS shall be 531120. Note that this service contract, if awarded, will be in full accordance with the requirements set forth in the memo. Property Management: The contractor shall provide an environment that meets the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement. It shall be approximately within a 6-mile radius of the Concord Town House, 22 Monument Square, Concord, MA (with the approximate coordinates being 42�27'40.1"N 71�20'55.0"W). (The agency may consider an environment outside of this 6-mile radius if it determines that it is in its best interest to do so.) It shall have roughly 30,000 square feet of office space; it shall contain 190 or more workstations, 6 to 8 private �office pods� or �booths� (each of a size sufficient to accommodate one individual), 4 small collaborative spaces (each of a size sufficient to accommodate up to 6 individuals), a commercial lactation pod, and 6 to 8 meeting rooms, with a personnel range of 151-175 individuals when fully operational, and potentially 176-200 individuals to meet future programmatic demands. It shall have a break area/dining area and a shared kitchen area that meet the requirements specified in the PWS. The parking lot or garage shall have a capacity sufficient for all personnel. Within the coworking space, the contractor shall provide a dedicated, private, exclusive fully enclosed office for the operational use of authorized DAF personnel, which meets the security, structural, and other specifications listed in the PWS. IT Support and Maintenance Services: The vendor shall provide IT support for the coworking space�s workstations and conference equipment. It shall provide on-site technical support staffing. It shall monitor the equipment and the IT infrastructure to ensure that equipment is free from defects, that equipment is operable, and that connectivity is maintained. If the vendor observes any actual or potential information security violations in the course of providing this support, it shall report them to the Government Security Manager. Administrative and Janitorial Services: The vendor shall ensure that restrooms are restocked and maintained, that the shared kitchen and kitchen appliances are maintained, that shared kitchen supplies are restocked (including the restocking of the commercial coffee machine and beverage dispenser), that meeting rooms, open seating areas, and other elements of the coworking space are maintained, shall provide front desk staffing, and shall otherwise administer the coworking space in accordance with commercial practices and with agency-specific needs. Software Licenses, Collaboration Licenses, Network Services, Power/Utility Services, and Commercial Wi-Fi: The contractor shall provide these services in accordance with the PWS. Hardware and Enclosures: The contractor shall install and maintain contractor-owned or contractor-leased hardware and equipment (e.g. printers) and shall install and maintain government-owned hardware and equipment (e.g. large-format displays and computer monitors) in accordance with the PWS. It shall permit the installation of a lockable, ventilated, government-owned IT equipment rack or wall-mounted communications cabinet within the dedicated space. This notice is not a solicitation and does not bind the agency in any way. If the agency opts to post a solicitation, it will only consider those bidders that are actively registered on SAM.gov at the time of issuance of the solicitation. Responses are due on Nov 2, 2026 at 12:00 pm EST, and should be emailed to Contract Specialist Steven C. Bodnar at steven.bodnar@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist Andrew C. St. Maurice at andrew.st_maurice@us.af.mil.

title: Request for Information - Enterprise Learning Management System (LMS) of Record with a Learning Experience Platform (LXP)
description: TSA has an opportunity to improve training delivery by strengthening training consistency and expanding flexible pathways that recognize prior experience. A more unified digital learning approach could also help balance compliance with reporting requirements with accessible, engaging microlearning for a globally dispersed, multigenerational workforce. The purpose of this program is to acquire and deploy an integrated, vendor-neutral digital learning ecosystem combining an authoritative Enterprise Learning Management System (LMS) of record with a modern Learning Experience Platform (LXP). title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE RELATED TO SEVERAL UPCOMING PROJECTS at WRIGHT-PATTERSON AFB, OHIO
description: ***21 October 2026 Update: The responses due date is being revised to 02 Novemeber at 12:00 P.M. Eastern Time. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE RELATED TO SEVERAL UPCOMING PROJECTS at WPAFB, OHIO Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) 1. PROJECT OVERVIEWS The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), in support of the United States Air Force (USAF), is conducting market research to identify interested and qualified industry partners for the design and construction of several upcoming construction projects at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. PROJECT 1: RENOVATE NASIC MAIN CAMPUS, PHASE 1, F/10853 - This project is renovation of 170,000 SF of Sensitive and/or Special Access Program spaces. The work consists of the full renovation of F/10853 through reconfiguration and interior renovation to create a network of administrative functions. The work shall be done in accordance with Intelligence Community Directive 705 (ICD 705) criteria and standards. The interior demolition consists of removal of all architectural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) elements including floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. Work includes replacement of building systems, reconfiguration of interior partitions, life safety systems, roof replacement, and envelope modification. The roofing system will be replaced with an energy-compliant system. Penetrations will be added to the building for daylighting, and the exterior envelope will be modified on first floor locations for mechanical rooms. All piping and sprinklers that are part of the current fire protection system are to be replaced. All domestic water, storm, and sanitary piping will be replaced. Additionally, this project includes cybersecurity measures. A corridor bridge connecting F/10828 and F/10856 over an existing loading dock is to be constructed. Personnel will require swing space during the renovation of F/10853. Swing space will be provided through existing available spaces throughout the NASIC IPC campus or via a temporary facility. It is critical that the sequencing of repair work be considered so that available spaces are not overwhelmed. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $160,000,000 PROJECT 2: Advanced Materials Research Laboratory � C2A - Construction of an approximately ~90,000 SF three-story laboratory and research facility, as well as the potential construction of a central utility plant for the Air Force Reach Labor Material and Manufacturing Directorate. New facility will consist of concrete, foundation, structural steel frame, masonry etc. Onsite gas boilers for heat and chilled water generation for cooling and lab processes. The interior shall consist of open inter-disciplinary collaboration labs with clean utilities, vibration isolation, precision HVAC and humidity controls, as well as fire protection/suppression, intrusion detections systems and medium voltage switchgear (i.e. 12,470 volts). Site work consists of utilities, sidewalks, parking, communications The new facility shall connect to existing facilities and demolitions of facility 20654. is part of this project. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $122,000,000 PROJECT 3: Compressor Research Facility Systems Modernization This project will modernize the Air Force Research Lab�s (AFRL) Compressor Research Facility (CRF) by replacing legacy drive and power equipment with a new 30,000-horsepower Variable Frequency Drive system to support engine component testing. The effort will deliver a fully integrated system that improves reliability, control, maintainability, and long-term test capability. Work includes replacement of the existing drive system with a new 30,000-horsepower VFD with active front end, a new 30,000-horsepower brushless synchronous motor, a new primary transformer, medium-voltage switchgear, protective relaying, and all associated interconnecting cables, bus work, grounding, and terminations. The project also includes the demolition and removal of legacy electrical and mechanical equipment; upgrades to controls, monitoring interfaces, cooling and ventilation systems, and supporting electrical infrastructure; and any required structural, foundation, enclosure, or fire/life-safety modifications needed to install and operate the new equipment. Additional work will include system integration, testing, commissioning, performance verification, operator and maintainer training, and delivery of technical data, recommended spare parts, and warranty support. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $25,000,000 PROJECT 4: Consolidate/Demo F/31240 This project will decentralize Area A heating by replacing the aging high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system fed from Building F/31240, Line A, and Line D with standalone boiler plants serving 49 facilities. The project supports administrative, warehouse, laboratory, hangar, and dormitory buildings that require year-round hot water for heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. Work includes facility surveys, evaluation of mechanical room capacity and code compliance, and determination of any needed interior renovations or limited additions to support the new equipment. The project also includes demolition of Building F/31240 and its boiler equipment, removal of above-ground HTHW piping and supports, and capping and abandonment of below-grade piping in place. New high-efficiency boiler systems, pumps, controls, and related accessories will be installed at affected facilities, with evaluation of both natural gas-fired and electric options. Additional work includes mechanical room modifications, make-up water assemblies where needed, upgrades to electrical, fire alarm, fire suppression, and direct digital control systems, and site restoration including pavement repair, grass restoration, and backfill and seeding at the demolished plant site. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $66,500,000 PROJECT 5: Consolidate/Demo West Ramp This project will decentralize heating for the West Ramp area at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base by replacing the existing high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system from Building F/34019 with standalone boiler plants serving 15 surrounding facilities. The effort addresses aging and degraded infrastructure supporting administrative, laboratory, and active hangar facilities that require year-round hot water for comfort heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. The project includes surveying each facility to determine boiler locations, evaluating mechanical room walls for code compliance, and assessing whether mechanical room expansions, electrical upgrades, or system improvements are needed to support the new equipment. Work includes demolition and removal of Building F/34019 and its internal boiler equipment, along with demolition of the exterior emergency generator, tank, piping, and all above-ground HTHW piping, supports, and foundations. Below-grade piping will be capped and abandoned in place. Each affected facility will receive new high-efficiency boiler systems, distribution pumps, controls, and related access

description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS code is 334519 - Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing, with an SBA small business size standard of 600 employees. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published. The purpose of this procurement is to acquire and install a fully automated, weight-based inventory management system, brand name or equal to PAR Excellence, for the VA Phoenix Healthcare System. The system is intended to provide accurate, real-time perpetual inventory visibility while minimizing end-user data entry and supporting timely replenishment of medical and surgical supplies. The anticipated requirement includes all equipment, scales, controllers, storage products, mounting hardware and accessories, software licenses, interfaces, implementation services, installation, configuration, testing, training, warranty, monitoring, maintenance, and technical support necessary to deliver a fully operational system at the facility's designated primary and secondary supply locations. For market-research and planning purposes, the anticipated configuration is approximately 26 PAR Bins Replenish software licenses, 3,571 scales of various types and capacities, 27 Ethernet replenishment controllers, related hardware accessories, storage bins, shelving, cabinets, mobile louvered panel units, and associated implementation and training services. Final quantities and configurations are subject to change. At a minimum, the proposed solution must provide an HL7 interface that communicates with the VA Generic Inventory Package (GIP) in VistA and must have an approved VA Information Technology Authority to Operate (ATO) at the time of offer. Contractors must be able to validate interoperability with VA GIP through the HL7 interface prior to award. The system must support unlimited users and multiple permission levels; provide access from multiple points on VA-furnished computers; produce Excel or text-delimited reports; display equipment and materials-management status; provide item-location, PAR-level analysis, consumption data, order, reconciliation, due-in/due-out, discrepancy, and inventory-value reporting; and generate pick-ticket information based on PAR levels, reorder points, and emergency stock levels. The system must be compatible with existing shelving, cabinets, carts, and other storage infrastructure; accommodate medical and surgical products of varying size, thickness, and weight, including products up to approximately 3 feet long by 2 feet wide and 20 pounds; and permit VA employees to recalibrate the system for different package quantities. The contractor must install and configure the required software on VA-furnished equipment, provide staff training, furnish a one-year license agreement with software upgrades, and provide 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year support. Support must include at least four remote equipment-functionality checks every 24 hours, response to service calls within 24 hours, and repair or replacement of covered equipment or hardware within 48 hours when damage or defect is not attributable to VA personnel. Installation is anticipated to begin no later than 70 days after contract award and be completed no later than 400 days after award, subject to facility deployment planning and required facility tasks. Deliverables will be shipped to VA Phoenix Healthcare System, Main Warehouse (ATTN: Prentiss Logan), 650 E Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012, with notice to the Contracting Officer's Representative five business days before shipment. The current independent planning estimate derived from the attached vendor quotation is $1,502,945.49, inclusive of turnkey installation. This amount is provided solely to describe the anticipated magnitude of the requirement for market-research purposes and does not constitute a Government estimate, commitment, or solicitation price. STATEMENT OF WORK 1. Background VA Phoenix Healthcare System has used cabinet-based Point of Use (POU) systems to manage inventory levels within our facility s supply areas. Our facility s current supply system process relies heavily on clinical staff entering quantities as they pull product. When they fail to enter, or enter incorrect quantities, our process fails. This leads to workload issues, as Supply Techs must be pulled from current duties to perform urgent resupply requests to affected areas. This also presents potential patient safety issues during emergency situations if stock is not available due to inaccurate stock level information. Further, the current supply process is labor and time intensive. This is compounded in times of heavy workload due to availability of supply personnel and/or hospital patient load, increasing risks associated with patient care / safety. VA Phoenix Healthcare System is looking for a fully automated weight-based inventory management system that does not require end users to input data or interface with the system to increase or decrease material items stocked or consumed by the user. The station requires a system that removes or heavily limits the amount of human interface required to maintain accurate and real time inventories. This creates a more accurate and efficient system while simultaneously addressing the patient safety / care concerns mentioned above, eliminating the frequent emergent supply requests created by inadequate inventory management systems. A fully automated weight-based inventory management system will augment the supply chain s management effectiveness and timeliness with resupply inventory while decreasing the workload of supply personnel. It will also improve the overall patient care throughout the facility, particularly in the cardiac catheterization and electrophysiology labs, by effectively maintaining appropriate periodic automatic replacement levels. 2. Scope The scope of this requirement is to obtain and install an automated inventory management system at VA Phoenix Healthcare System, ensure system is fully operational, and fully train staff to be knowledgeable on the use of system. This is a brand name or equal requirement; a Fully Automated Weight-Based Inventory Management System or equal to PAR Excellence. Contractors must provide a brand name or equal that meets or exceeds the physical, functional, and performance of listed characteristics described in this Statement of Work. title: J066--Epredia Vega and SlideMate Systems Maintenance Support Services for the Greater Los Angeles VA Healthcare System
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Government intends to award a firm fixed price, sole source contract in accordance with RFO FAR 6.103 1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, and in conjunction with RFO FAR 12.201-1, Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items. This requirement is for the maintenance support services for multiple Epredia Vega and SlideMate Laboratory systems located within the Greater Los Angeles VA Healthcare System. The intended source is Richard-Allan Scientific LLC / Epredia, the original equipment manufacturer (OEM). In accordance with RFO FAR Part 6, contracts awarded using this authority must be supported by written Justification & Approval (J&A), as described in RFO FAR 6.301 and 6.104. As applicable, the approved justification will be posted within fourteen (14) days after award pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3204(f) and 41 U.S.C. 3304(f). The Government will consider capability statements received by the closing date of this synopsis. The Government s decision whether to compete with this requirement, based on responses received, is solely at its discretion. Any information submitted will be used strictly to determine whether competitive procurement is appropriate. The applicable North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance, with a size standard of $34.0 million. Description of the Requirement (Draft Statement of Work (SOW)) Scope: The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, supplies, parts, software (needed for the general operation of the equipment), tools, equipment, travel, transportation expenses and other related costs to provide licensing for software use and corrective maintenance services on the Epredia SlideMate and Vega systems to the participating facilities listed herein of the Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 22. The Epredia SlideMate and Vega system enables on demand labeling of Anatomic Pathology slides and cassettes. Period of Performance: Base year followed by four, one year option periods. General Requirement: All work shall be in accordance with manufacturer s instructions, including, but not limited to, adjustments, calibration, cleaning, lubrication, testing, disassembly, checkout, and replacement of worn and/or defective parts. The above shall be performed as necessary as required to keep equipment in optimal working condition. This refers to the equipment listed in Table 1 below: EE# Serial Number Equipment PM Frequency 243778 5000-E-202-0724 Vega System Annual - July 255886 5000-E-193-0724 Vega System Annual - July 246254 SPA03245532 SlideMate System N/A 246257 SPA03245523 SlideMate System N/A 246255 SPA02245478 SlideMate System N/A 246259 SPA02245473 SlideMate System N/A 246258 SPA02245470 SlideMate System N/A 243777 SPA06245677 SlideMate System N/A 243776 SPA05245627 SlideMate System N/A Table 1: Equipment included as part of this requirement Contractor shall provide OEM gold service plan coverage or equivalent on Vega Systems listed in Table 1. Plan coverage shall include all replacement parts, labor, and travel expenses for any unscheduled service visit. Includes one hour of live lab retraining annually. One preventive maintenance visit per coverage year. Loaner instruments shall be included based on instrument type and availability. Contractor shall provide OEM gold swap plan coverage or equivalent on SlideMate systems listed in Table 1. Plan coverage shall include swap replacement of SlideMate unit requiring repair with a refurbished replacement at no cost. Replacement units must be shipped within 48 hours depending on request timing. Corrective Maintenance / Repair Services: The Contractor shall conduct corrective maintenance/repair services as required by the Government. All equipment must also be maintained in such a condition that will satisfy the requirements of the Joint Commission. The Contractor may request a copy of the JC standards from the Program POC. The Contractor shall provide all travel and transportation expenses at no cost to the Government. The Contractor shall provide phone technical support from 7:00AM to 3:30PM PST. The Contractor shall provide all corrective maintenance repair and replacement parts at no cost to the Government. The Contractor shall provide a detailed service report to the Program POC within 10 business days of corrective maintenance. Replacement Parts: Only standard new or like-new parts shall be furnished by the Contractor. All parts shall be of current manufacture and shall have versatility with presently installed equipment. All major components and parts furnished shall carry the manufacturer s standard commercial warranty. All newly installed parts will become property of the Government. Replaced parts are to be disposed by the Contractor after approval of Program POC. All worn or defective parts are to be replaced at no cost to the Government. Operating and consumable supplies are not included in this contract. The Veterans Affairs Healthcare Facility shall not furnish parts, service manuals and/or test equipment for the performance of this contract. It is the responsibility of the Contractor to bring appropriate equipment and/or supplies necessary to complete the work as required. Participating Facility: VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System 11301 Wilshire Blvd Los Angeles, CA 90073 Hours of Work: This contract is a full-service contract to include all necessary scheduled service calls five (5) days per week, Monday through Friday, 7:00 am 5:00 pm, excluding National holidays. Telephone support services are available at no additional cost to the Government. Any service performed during other than normal work hours must have prior approval and coordinated with the Program POC or CO. Qualification: Personnel performing maintenance and repair services must be fully qualified, competent Field Service Engineers (FSE) who has been trained to perform work on the specific equipment in accordance with the original manufacturer s PMI/ repair procedures. Fully qualified is defined as factory-trained or equivalent and experienced to work on the equipment assigned. Service: Service shall include software updates needed for the general operation of the equipment. At the completion of PMI on each equipment and ensure upon departure that the equipment is in optimal working condition. Service also includes all necessary intervening service calls required to replace any worn or defective parts needed due to instrument failure and maintain equipment in optimum operating condition. Intervening services shall be rendered as directed by the Program POC. Any call back for service request for the same type of malfunction shall be at no charge to the Government. Intervening Service Call: When repairs are needed between regular scheduled service, such repairs are rendered as directed only by the Program POC or the Contracting Officer (CO). These repairs shall be verbally directed to the Contractor s employees, requested in writing, be transmitted electronically, by telephone, or any manner consistent with accepted commercial business practices. Additional Requirement: Contractor shall ensure all equipment is in optimal working condition at the expiration date of the contract. Contractor personnel that perform changes, updates, or retrofits made on any component, system, or equipment will log it in the station equipment manual. Contractor will maintain all manufactures manual necessary to perform maintenance. Submission of Reports: The Contractor shall submit a complete field service report (FSR) electronically to the Program POC within 7 calendar days of the work being completed. title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.
