REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) BUILDING 215 ADVANCED MEASUREMENT LABORATORY (AML) CLEANROOM REPAIR AND HEPA FILTER REPLACEMENT Solicitation/Reference No.: 1333ND26RNB190014 1. PURPOSE OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201 to obtain industry feedback concerning the scope, schedule, phasing, cleanroom outage requirements, technical and performance risks, and estimated construction cost associated with the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory (AML) Cleanroom Repair and HEPA Filter Replacement project. NIST previously solicited this requirement under Solicitation No. 1333ND26RNB190014. NIST did not receive an acceptable offer under that solicitation. NIST is therefore reassessing the requirement and acquisition approach before determining whether and how to resolicit the project. NIST is particularly interested in identifying aspects of the requirement that may materially affect industry participation, constructability, schedule feasibility, pricing, risk, or the ability of contractors to submit competitive proposals. Industry is encouraged to provide candid feedback and to identify recommended changes that could improve constructability, competition, schedule feasibility, cost certainty, and overall project execution while continuing to meet NIST�s mission and cleanroom operational requirements. 2. RFI / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE THIS RFI IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND ACQUISITION PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR OTHER SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses to this RFI. Responses will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as offers or proposals that can be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI or for participating in any follow-up discussions. This RFI does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government�s ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be used by NIST in developing or revising the acquisition strategy, statement of work, specifications, schedule, phasing requirements, outage requirements, Government cost estimate, and future solicitation. Respondents should clearly identify and mark any proprietary, confidential, or commercially sensitive information contained in their responses. Respondents should avoid including proprietary information unless necessary to provide a meaningful response. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND The project involves repair and modernization work within the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory cleanroom located at the NIST Gaithersburg Campus. The AML cleanroom encompasses approximately 1,800 square meters and includes approximately 750 square meters of Class 100 cleanroom space. The facility supports sensitive NIST research activities and contains specialized and, in some instances, irreplaceable scientific equipment. The project generally includes, but is not limited to: Replacement of approximately 1,200 terminal supply HEPA filters; Repair and/or modification of HEPA filter connections; Testing, balancing, certification, and recertification of affected HEPA filters and cleanroom spaces; Replacement of approximately 70 variable air volume (VAV) terminal units; Replacement of approximately 54 airflow monitoring devices; Installation of approximately 32 exhaust air control valves; Modification and repair of associated ductwork; Rebalancing of associated air-handling and exhaust systems; Verification and repair, as required, of existing capped ductwork; Controls-related work; Cleaning, testing, balancing, commissioning, and cleanroom certification associated with each affected area; and Protection of existing cleanroom spaces, research operations, and sensitive scientific equipment throughout construction. Detailed project drawings, specifications, and/or relevant portions of the previously issued solicitation may be attached to this RFI or otherwise made available through SAM.gov for purposes of industry review. 4. CURRENT PHASING AND OUTAGE CONCEPT NIST�s previous acquisition strategy was developed to minimize disruption to ongoing research operations by performing the work through phased cleanroom outages rather than shutting down the entire cleanroom for the duration of construction. The previous requirement contemplated 19 construction phases consisting of 18 Critical Cleanroom Outage Phases and one Non-Critical Phase. For each Critical Cleanroom Outage Phase, the contemplated outage period was approximately nine calendar days, generally structured as follows: Outage/construction activities begin at approximately 7:00 p.m. on Friday; Work proceeds continuously, including 24-hour-per-day/seven-day-per-week operations, as necessary; Construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification are completed during the outage period; and The affected cleanroom area is required to achieve Ready for Re-Occupancy by approximately 7:00 a.m. on the second following Monday. Ready for Re-Occupancy generally means that required construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification have been completed; the affected area is operationally capable of supporting its intended use without material restriction; and no deficiencies remain that materially impair safe occupancy or cleanroom operations. title: Governor Control Programming
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) at the Libby Dam Project (17877 Hwy 37, Libby, MT 59923) is modernizing its Main Unit Governors by replacing existing pressure switches with pressure transducers on five (5) units. The objective of this contract is to procure specialized governor control programming, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) / Human Machine Interface (HMI) development, and commissioning support from the contractor to accommodate this hardware change. This is a turnkey requirement; the Contractor assumes full responsibility for understanding the existing system logic and delivering a fully functional, updated programming solution with no technical assistance from the Government. Work shall be accomplished on a rolling outage basis as units become available, spanning from the Contract Award Date through August 30, 2027. Work will occur across remote and on-site location, structured as follows: Tasks 1 & 3 (Remote): Contractor's Facility. Task 2 (On-Site Commissioning): Libby Dam Project, 17155 HWY 37, Libby, MT 59923-9703 Quoters must submit a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) quote for all contract line item numbers (CLINs). Incomplete quotes will be ineligible for award. To be considered for award, interested parties must submit an email quote package directly adhering to the following rules: E-mail Address: Quotes must be emailed to the Contract Specialist, Londres Medranda, at londres.medranda@usace.army.mil SAM Registration: Offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of quote submission and maintain it through performance and final payment. Inquiries & Questions: Questions must be sent via email to the Contract Specialist no later than five (5) working days prior to the quote due date. This ensures sufficient time for the Government to publish amendments on SAM.gov.

title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR PROJECT LABOR AGGREEMENTS (PLAs) TO COASTAL STORM RISK MANAGEMENT (CSRM) FOR CAPE MAY TO LOWER TOWNSHIP, NEW JERSEY, BRIGANTINE INLET TO GREAT EGG HARBOR INLET (ABSECON ISLAND), NEW JERSEY, AND BARNEGAT INLET TO LITTLE EGG, INLET
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Cape May To Lower Township, New Jersey, Brigantine Inlet To Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), New Jersey, And Barnegat Inlet To Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), New Jersey area. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Cape May to Lower Township, NJ (Navigation Mitigation � Beachfill): Work for the beachfill placement dredging will require a hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s). The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge material up to a depth of -40 ft NAVD88 and to transport the dredged sand to the designated areas approximately 2.6 miles away. The project for navigation mitigation (beach nourishment) is located on the Atlantic coast of New Jersey, extending from the Cape May Inlet southwest jetty to the 3rd Ave terminal groin in Cape May City. It includes the communities of the City of Cape May and Lower Township, and the US Coast Guard Training Center. The contract work will consist of a base bid to conduct pre-placement condition surveys and pump/place 600,000 cubic yards of sand from two borrow areas approximately 2.6 miles south of the Cape May Inlet jetties onto the beach at 2 locations: Area 1 (540,000 cu yds), the US Coast Guard Training Center and Area 2 (60,000 cu yds), Wilmington Ave. Options to place additional sand (100,000 cu yds) from the same borrow areas to achieve the full project design template at these same two beach locations will also be included. Sand must come from the offshore borrow areas. Trucking-in sand will not be permitted under this contract. All work under the contract must be completed no later than 1 March 2028. Brigantine Inlet to Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 1,500,000 cubic yards of beachfill, along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Absecon Island, Atlantic County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Atlantic City, Ventnor, Margate, and Longport. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compliant dune crossovers; planting dune grass; installing sand fencing; the repair or extension of existing storm water outfalls and drainage structures; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures or fill to accommodate the beachfill and dunes. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas, which are shown on the contract drawings, located within and adjacent to the Absecon Inlet in the Atlantic Ocean, and a separate designated area located approximately 2 � 3 miles offshore of Absecon Island in the Atlantic Ocean. Barnegat Inlet to Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 2,000,000 cubic yards of beachfill to repair the dune and berm system along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Long Beach Island, Ocean County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Long Beach Township, Borough of Harvey Cedars, Borough of Surf City, Borough of Ship Bottom, and Borough of Beach Haven. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compatible dune crossovers; planting dune grass; providing sand fencing; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures to accommodate the beachfill, dunes and other project features. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas located approximately 2-3 miles offshore of Long Beach Island in the Atlantic Ocean, and/or the Little Egg Inlet as designated on the contract drawings. The solicitation is expected to be available in FY2027. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: (a) Project Labor Agreement (PLA) is a tool that agencies may use to promote economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Pursuant to Executive Order 14063, agencies are encouraged to consider requiring the use of project labor agreements in connection with large-scale construction projects. (b) An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will (1) Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and (2) Be consistent with law. Reference: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. (i) Requested are responses to the following: 1) Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. 2) Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 3) Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 4) Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 5) Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 6) Identify any additional information you believe the Government should take into consideration regarding the use of a PLA on the referenced project. 7) Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is not included in the solicitation? 8) What are the likely cost impacts, if any, to your bid/proposal price if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. (ii) The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): 1) Project Name and Location: 2) Detailed Project Description: 3) Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost: 4) Was the project completed on time? 5) Number of craft trades present on the project: 6) Was a PLA used? 7) Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Responses shall be submitted via email to Terri Adams

title: Instrument Landing Structure (ILS)
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT notice; a market survey for information only, to be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor SAM for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The acquisition strategy will be determined based on responses received from this notice and/or other market research methods. The planned acquisition strategy will be posted in SAM upon completion of market research analysis. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of industry, to include the Small Business Community: Small Business, Section 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUB-Zone), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), or Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB). All are highly encouraged to respond. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, intends to solicit and award a contract for site and preparatory construction work associated with an unmanned ILS. The anticipated acquisition will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price (FFP), design-bid-build (DBB), definitive contract. The procurement will be conducted in accordance with RFO 15.103-3, using the Highest Technically Rated with a Fair and Reasonable Price evaluation approach. The Government is seeking experienced firms to perform site preparation and construction work associated with an unmanned ILS site. The site will accommodate three primary elements of Government-Furnished, Government-Installed (GFGI) electronic equipment under a separate contract: a directional localizer, a glide slope indicator, and radio marker beacons. The scope of work includes demolition; rerouting existing drainage systems and utilities, as necessary; installation of new utility service lines; gate installation; and site filling and finish grading to support the subsequent installation of the ILS equipment. The target price range for this project is between $7.8M and $8.4M. This project is subject to Minor Military Construction (MILCON) funding and Statutory Limitations - Offerors are advised that this requirement is funded as an Unspecified Minor MILCON (UMMC) project in accordance with (IAW) 10 U.S.C. � 2805. Because this project relies on Minor MILCON funding, total project costs are strictly limited by federal statute. Proposals must and will be evaluated IAW this statutory policy. The Government cannot and will not make an award if the proposed price exceeds the applicable legal thresholds for UMMC projects. The estimated Period of Performance is 365 calendar days. title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YRBM-50
description: 22 October 2026- The purpose of amendment 0003 is to extend the proposal due date from 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 2 November 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. ____________________ 14 October 2026-The purpose of amendment 0002 is to extend the RFC due date from 8 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 15 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT and the proposal due date from 19 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. Also, the Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachment 6 References and Drawings have been updated as of 13 October 2026. ____________________ 17 September 2026- Reason for amendment 0001 is to add additional ship check date, extend the deadline for clarifications and solicitation end date. See section L. ____________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. This is a 100% Small Business set-aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 336611, size standard 1,300 employees. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, DE (CSRM - Beachfill), Fenwick Island, DE (CSRM � Beachfill), and Rehoboth Beach & Dewey Beach, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): areas. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, DE (CSRM - Beachfill): The work for the Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, CRSM projects will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 532,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach to the original design template and approximately 165,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. Borrow Area E will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since Borrow Area E is located approximately two to three miles offshore of the Town of South Bethany. Fenwick Island, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): The work for the Fenwick Island, CRSM project will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 207,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Fenwick Island to the original design template and approximately 60,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. The Fenwick Island borrow area will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since the Fenwick Borrow Area is located approximately one to three miles offshore of the Town of Fenwick Island. Rehoboth Beach & Dewey Beach, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): The work for the Rehoboth Beach to Dewey Beach, CRSM projects will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 390,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Rehoboth Beach and Dewey Beach to the design template and approximately 120,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. Borrow Area B will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper dredge due to the four to six mile transit distance that must be made in the Atlantic Ocean to travel to and from the sand borrow area. The solicitation is expected to be available in FY2027. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: (a) Project Labor Agreement (PLA) is a tool that agencies may use to promote economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Pursuant to Executive Order 14063, agencies are encouraged to consider requiring the use of project labor agreements in connection with large-scale construction projects. (b) An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will (1) Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and (2) Be consistent with law. Reference: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. (i) Requested are responses to the following: 1) Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. 2) Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 3) Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 4) Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 5) Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 6) Identify any additional information you believe the Government should take into consideration regarding the use of a PLA on the referenced project. 7) Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is not included in the solicitation? 8) What are the likely cost impacts, if any, to your bid/proposal price if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. (ii) The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): 1) Project Name and Location 2) Detailed Project Description 3) Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost 4) Was the project completed on time? 5) Number of craft trades present on the project 6) Was a PLA used? 7) Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Responses shall be submitted via email to Melissa Vaughn at melissa.a.vaughn@usace.army.mil and Ros Shoemaker at rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil no later than 3:00 PM EDT on 15 September 2026. The email should be titled: Delaware CSRM PLA Response This is NOT a Request for Proposal and does not constitute any commitment by the Government. title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YRBM-50
description: 22 October 2026- The purpose of this amendment is to extend the proposal due date from 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 2 November 2026 at 12:00 PM PT.____________________ 14 October 2026-The purpose of this amendment is to extend the RFC due date from 8 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 15 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT and the proposal due date from 19 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. Also, the Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachment 6 References and Drawings have been updated as of 13 October 2026. ____________________ 17 September 2026- Reason for amendment 0001 is to add additional ship check date, extend the deadline for clarifications and solicitation end date. See section L. ____________________The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. This is a 100% Small Business set-aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 336611, size standard 1,300 employees. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Notice of Opportunity (NOO) U.S. Army Reserve, 88th Readiness Division Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)
description: U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). These efforts align with statutory requirements under 10 U.S.C. � 2911 for energy security and resilience, and 42 U.S.C. � 8287 through the Department of Energy�s (DOE) Fourth-Generation Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Responses to this NOO must be received no later than 02 November, 3:00 p.m. (Ft. Belvoir, VA local time). Responses must be completed and submitted to the following email mailbox: DLAEnergy-ESPC@dla.mil

The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record.
